headline: Kākāpō Rising: World's Heaviest Parrot Hits 300-Bird Milestone
meta_description: New Zealand's kākāpō population has surpassed 300 birds for the first time in 75 years, with 90 chicks born this breeding season.
summary_short: The kākāpō, Earth's heaviest parrot species, has reached a population milestone not seen in three-quarters of a century.
body:
The population of the world's heaviest parrot, the kākāpō, has surpassed 300 birds for the first time in 75 years. This milestone comes after a successful breeding season that produced 90 chicks.

The New Zealand native represents one of conservation's most determined comeback stories. Each chick born represents real progress in bringing the species back from the brink. The achievement marks a turning point in decades-long efforts to restore this extraordinary bird to sustainable numbers.
quick_facts: Kākāpō is the world's heaviest parrot species
Population now exceeds 300 birds for first time in 75 years
90 chicks hatched in latest breeding season
